planting.note: Plant in fall or early spring in rich, well-drained soil in partial to full shade; Cherry Blossom is part of the Winter Jewels breeding series, with soft pale pink single flowers blooming in late winter to early spring.

directions: Plant in rich, well-drained, humus-rich soil in partial to full shade, keeping soil evenly moist while the plant establishes. Cherry Blossom is part of the acclaimed Winter Jewels hellebore breeding series, producing rounded, outward-facing, single flowers in soft, blush pink reminiscent of its namesake tree blossoms, held above leathery, evergreen, deeply divided foliage. Like other Lenten roses it blooms very early, often pushing through late-season snow or hard frost, providing reliable color in the shade garden when little else is flowering. Remove tattered old foliage in late winter just before bloom to showcase the flowers at their best, and site it away from areas where pets or children graze, since all parts of the plant are toxic if ingested.
sources: Northwest Garden Nursery — Winter Jewels hellebore breeding

common_name: Gold Carpet Heucherella (Low Spreading Gold Foliage Foamy Bells)

planting.note: Plant divisions in spring in humus-rich, well-drained soil in partial to full shade; Gold Carpet spreads by stolons into a low, dense groundcover mat, spreading more actively than clump-forming heucherella cultivars.

directions: Plant in humus-rich, well-drained soil in partial to full shade; consistent moisture combined with good drainage keeps the shallow root system healthy. Gold Carpet spreads by stolons into a low, dense mat of bright chartreuse-gold, maple-like leaves, functioning as a true groundcover rather than the tidy mound habit typical of most heucherella cultivars, making it useful for filling in bare shaded ground beneath trees or along a woodland path. Small, airy white flower spikes appear above the foliage in late spring but are secondary to the season-long carpet of golden leaves. Water regularly during summer heat, and divide or thin the spreading mat as needed to keep it within bounds or to propagate additional plants for other areas of the garden.

common_name: Sunspot Heucherella (Gold Foliage with Red Center)

planting.note: Plant divisions in spring in humus-rich, well-drained soil in partial to full shade; Sunspot pairs bright gold foliage with a contrasting red central blotch that spreads along the leaf veins.

directions: Plant in humus-rich, well-drained soil in partial to full shade; consistent moisture combined with good drainage keeps the shallow root system healthy. Sunspot bears bright gold, deeply lobed leaves marked with a bold red central blotch that bleeds outward along the veins, a high-contrast pattern that intensifies with cooler weather and some morning sun, forming a dense, low mound. Small, airy white flower spikes rise above the foliage in late spring but are secondary to the vivid, season-long foliage color. Water regularly during summer heat to keep the foliage from scorching, and divide congested clumps every three to four years in spring to maintain vigor and a tidy habit.
